probes.question: What did Jenner use to protect people from smallpox?
options: Material from the milder disease cowpox

probes.question: The word 'vaccine' comes from a term meaning...

image.alt: A 19th-century oil painting of Edward Jenner vaccinating a young child held by its mother in a cottage interior

panels.text: In Edward Jenner's day, smallpox killed around 10% of the global population.
Jenner suspected that cowpox, a much milder disease, protected people from smallpox.
On 14 May 1796 he tested the idea on James Phipps, the eight-year-old son of his gardener, using pus from cowpox blisters on the hands of a milkmaid named Sarah Nelmes.
Jenner called the cowpox variolae vaccinae, 'pustules of the cow'. That is where the words vaccine and vaccination come from. His 1798 Inquiry described how cowpox protected against smallpox.
